name: Vercel
summary: Vercel hosts frontend and full-stack web apps with automatic deployments from Git, built by the creators of Next.js.

free_plan_covers.note: Free Hobby plan includes 100GB bandwidth and 1M function calls a month, enough for roughly 1,000 typical monthly users.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Pro plan is $20 per team member per month and includes $20 of usage credit, 1TB transfer, and 10M edge requests.

portability.note: Next.js code itself is portable, but Vercel's cron jobs, ISR cache, and Blob storage are proprietary and need rework elsewhere.

runtime_model.note: Backend code runs as Vercel Functions (serverless, with an optional Fluid compute pooling model), not a persistent server process.

persistent_disk.note: Functions have no writable persistent filesystem; use Vercel Blob or an external database or storage service instead.

long_lived_connections.note: Vercel Functions cannot hold WebSocket connections open; Vercel's own guide recommends a third-party realtime service instead.

background_workers.note: There is no always-on worker service type; only request-triggered or cron-triggered functions are available.

scheduled_jobs.note: Native Cron Jobs are supported, up to 100 per project. Hobby plan cron jobs can only run once a day; Pro allows every minute.

free_plan_commercial_use.note: Vercel's pricing page states the Hobby plan is for personal, non-commercial use only; Pro is required to sell a product.

framework_support.note: Next.js is built by Vercel with full SSR and ISR support; static React and Vite apps deploy cleanly; SvelteKit works fully via the official adapter-vercel.

setup.step: Sign up at vercel.com and install the Vercel CLI, or just use the dashboard.
Import your Git repository (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket) as a new Vercel project.
Vercel auto-detects your framework's build command; add any environment variables in Project Settings.
Click Deploy. Every push to your main branch redeploys automatically, and pull requests get their own preview URL.

builder_notes: Hobby plan forbids commercial use and limits cron jobs to once a day; budget for the $20/month Pro plan if the app will make money or needs frequent cron.
Do not rely on WebSockets in Vercel Functions; use a third-party realtime service (Ably, Pusher) or a separate always-on server for chat or live features.
There is no persistent filesystem; store uploads in Vercel Blob or an external service, not local disk.
